    Python API¶

    terraingen ¶

    TerrainGen: scientific terrain generation for planetary surfaces.

    TerrainGen's log records go to the standard logging module on loggers named "terraingen.", such as "terraingen.craters". TerrainGen itself only produces records at or above set_log_level(), which defaults to "warning"; lower it to see timing statements.

    Functions:

    Name Description
    use_python_logging

    Send TerrainGen's log records to the logging module (done on import).

    MATERIAL_CLASSES module-attribute ¶

    MATERIAL_CLASSES: int = 5

    int([x]) -> integer int(x, base=10) -> integer

    Convert a number or string to an integer, or return 0 if no arguments are given. If x is a number, return x.int(). For floating-point numbers, this truncates towards zero.

    If x is not a number or if base is given, then x must be a string, bytes, or bytearray instance representing an integer literal in the given base. The literal can be preceded by '+' or '-' and be surrounded by whitespace. The base defaults to 10. Valid bases are 0 and 2-36. Base 0 means to interpret the base from the string as an integer literal.

    int('0b100', base=0) 4

    AlbedoDetail ¶

    AlbedoDetail()

    Sub-cell detail added to an albedo map: octaves of noise carrying the map's measured roughness (or hurst) one octave down at a time, times scale.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    enabled bool

    Adds fractal detail below the map's resolution; off leaves the interpolated map as it is.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How octaves of detail too fine for the sample spacing fade out.
    hurst float | None

    Hurst exponent used instead of the one measured from the map; lower values keep more contrast at fine scales. Unset uses the measured one. Must be from 0 to 1.
    octaves int

    Octaves of detail, from half the map's cell size down, each half the wavelength of the one before. Must be from 1 to 16.
    scale float

    Factor on the RMS of every octave; 0 adds no detail, higher values give a more mottled albedo. Must not be negative.
    seed int

    Seed of the detail noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same roughness.

    How fully the layer covers (x, y) with its material, in [0, 1]. spacing is the sample spacing in meters; what reads the ground beneath needs a positive one and ground, such as terrain.beneath(n) beneath layer n of a Terrain, which also gives the surface and source.

    BedformOptions ¶

    BedformOptions()

    Ripples and dunes: wavelength and height (m), crests across wind_azimuth_deg(degrees counter-clockwise from +x), covering cover of the ground in fields field_size meters across.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    azimuth_spread_deg float

    Largest difference of each field's wind from the azimuth, in degrees. Must not be negative. Unit: deg.
    cover float

    Share of the ground under bedform fields; 0 gives no bedforms. Must be from 0 to 0.9.
    exposure ExposureParams | None

    Leaves out fields whose centers lie on bedrock, the likelier the barer the ground, as sand settles in lows; unset disables it.
    exposure_spacing float

    Spacing in meters the ground is read at for the exposure field. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How bedforms too fine for the sample spacing fade out, by samples per wavelength.
    field_size float

    Typical width of a bedform field, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    height float

    Trough-to-crest height, in meters, scaled with each field's wavelength. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    lee_fraction float

    Share of a wavelength the lee face takes: 0.5 is symmetric, lower values give a steeper lee face. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    seed int

    Seed of the fields and their crests; changing it gives a different layout of the same statistics.
    sinuosity float

    How far a crest wanders along its length, in wavelengths; 0 gives straight crests. Must not be negative.
    source_resolves_px float | None

    Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the bedforms, by their wavelength: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive. Unit: px.
    wavelength float

    Crest-to-crest spacing, in meters; each field's varies from 0.8 to 1.2 times it. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    wind_azimuth_deg float

    Direction the wind blows toward, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); crests lie across it. Unit: deg.

    BlastZone ¶

    BlastZone()

    The zone around a lander its engine scoured (Clegg et al. 2014): area m^2 brighter by change on average, elongated along heading_deg, in a halo reaching halo_reach times as far, around a dark core of core_radius m.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    area float

    Area of the blast zone in m^2; measured: Apollo 18,725 to 53,872 (mean 28,785), Luna 987 to 3355 (mean 2100), Surveyor 131 to 279 (mean 215), Chang'e-3 2530. Must be positive. Unit: m^2.
    change float

    Mean reflectance change over the zone relative to undisturbed ground at 30 degrees phase; measured +3.4% to +13.2%, Apollo mean +10.9%. Must be above -1.
    core_change float

    Reflectance change of the dark core; -15% to -30% at the Apollo sites. Must be above -1.
    core_radius float

    Radius in meters of the darker core beneath the engine and around the crew's tracks; 0 for none, a few meters at the Apollo sites. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    elongation float

    Long over short axis of the zone; Apollo about 1.14, Chang'e-3 about 1.74. Must be at least 1.
    halo_change float

    Reflectance change of the fainter halo beyond the zone; +4% at Chang'e-3. Must be above -1.
    halo_reach float

    How far the halo reaches over the zone's own reach; 1 for no halo. Must be at least 1.
    heading_deg float

    Direction of the long axis, degrees counter-clockwise from east, such as along the final approach. Unit: deg.
    raggedness float

    Share of the zone's radius that lobes of its edge pull in by. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    seed int

    Varies the edge's lobes.
    x float

    Surface x of the lander.
    y float

    Surface y of the lander.

    area: float

    BlendShape ¶

    Bases: enum.Enum

    How a weight falls from 1 to 0.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    GAUSSIAN

    Gaussian falloff with sigma a third of the band, rescaled to end at zero.
    LINEAR

    Straight ramp: continuous, with kinks at both ends.
    SMOOTHERSTEP

    Quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: continuous slope and curvature, the smoothest join.
    SMOOTHSTEP

    Cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3: continuous slope across the transition.

    GAUSSIAN class-attribute ¶

    GAUSSIAN = 3

    BoulderEjecta ¶

    BoulderEjecta()

    Boulders thrown out by craters at least min_crater_diameter across (or deep enough to reach bedrock under regolith_thickness): extra coverage near the rim, falling off to reach radii, fading as the crater ages.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    aging EjectaAging

    How a crater's blocks wear away with time, so that few are left around old craters.
    aging_exponent float

    With age aging, the exponent of (1 - age / lifetime); higher values strip blocks from craters sooner. Must not be negative.
    coverage float | None

    Golombek-Rapp k, the fraction of ground covered by blocks at the rim of a fresh crater; unset is 0.1. Only golombek_rapp ejecta sizes use it, so set it only with them. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    decay_radii float

    With the exponential profile, the e-folding distance of the blocks outside the rim, in crater radii. Must be positive.
    distribution SizeFrequencyDistribution

    Sizes per m^2 of the blocks at the rim of a fresh crater, in place of Golombek-Rapp blocks of coverage; None for those.
    excavation_depth_ratio float

    Depth of excavation over crater diameter; with the regolith thickness it sets the smallest crater that throws blocks. Must be above 0 and at most 1.
    floor_share float

    With the exponential profile, the crater floor's share of the rim's blocks. Must be from 0 to 1.
    gravity float | None

    Surface gravity in m/s^2: with the regolith thickness, it limits how far blocks are thrown, after Bart and Melosh (2010). Unset applies no such limit. Must be positive.
    lifetime_gyr float

    With age aging, the crater age in Gyr at which a crater keeps no blocks. Must be positive. Unit: Gyr.
    min_crater_diameter float | None

    Smallest crater, in meters, that throws blocks out; unset with no regolith thickness, no crater throws blocks. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    min_freshness float

    With freshness aging, the freshness (current over fresh depth) at or below which a crater keeps no blocks. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    profile EjectaProfile

    How the share of a crater's blocks falls off with distance from its center.
    reach float

    Distance from the crater's center, in crater radii, beyond which it adds no blocks. Must be above 1.
    regolith_thickness float | None

    Regolith thickness in meters: craters smaller than it over the excavation depth ratio dig no boulder and throw no blocks. Unset ignores the regolith. Must be positive. Unit: m.

    A layer of only boulders (ManualBoulder), posed and drawn as options says, with generate_random off and its manual replaced.

    material_cover_at method descriptor ¶

    material_cover_at() -> float

    material_cover_at(self, x: float, y: float, spacing: float = 0.0, ground: terraingen._terraingen.Ground | None = None) -> float

    How fully the layer covers (x, y) with its material, in [0, 1]. spacing is the sample spacing in meters; what reads the ground beneath needs a positive one and ground, such as terrain.beneath(n) beneath layer n of a Terrain, which also gives the surface and source.

    unresolved_cover_at method descriptor ¶

    unresolved_cover_at() -> tuple[float, float]

    unresolved_cover_at(self, x: float, y: float, spacing: float, ground: terraingen._terraingen.Ground | None = None) -> tuple[float, float]

    The share of a sample spacing meters across at (x, y) that boulders too small to resolve cover: (mean, variance), with the ground beneath them as for abundance_at.

    BoulderLayerOptions ¶

    BoulderLayerOptions()

    A boulder layer's settings: their sizes; patches, clusters, ejecta and bedrock shape where they lie; pose how each sits; rendering how they are drawn.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    bedrock BoulderBedrock

    Extra boulders where the ground beneath is bedrock.
    cache_boulders int

    Most generated boulders the layer keeps cached between queries.
    clusters BoulderClusters

    Clusters of the boulders between craters around scattered centers; off unless share is set.
    completeness SurfaceField

    Diameter (m) from which manual is a complete catalog at each point.
    density_map DensityMap | None

    (self) -> terraingen._terraingen.DensityMap | None
    ejecta BoulderEjecta

    Blocks thrown out by craters of every top-level crater layer before this one that dug into boulder, densest at the rim and thinning outward; none with generate_random off.
    fade ResolutionFade

    Which boulders are drawn into the heightmap by their size in output samples (pixels): the first count is the smallest drawn (2 by default, the fewest that resolve a boulder) and the second the size from which they are drawn in full. Smaller boulders exist only in the boulder lists and 3D models.
    fillet BoulderFillet

    Regolith piled against each boulder's base, around relief and models alike; off unless height_share is set.
    fragmentation BoulderFragmentation | None

    Boulders broken by wear into pieces that replace them, split and then scattered as rubble; leave it out for none to break.
    generate_random bool

    Draws random boulders from the size distribution, between craters and around them; off places only the manual boulders, and the sizes, coverage and ejecta go unused.
    ground_spacing float

    Spacing in meters at which the layer reads the ground beneath it, for the exposure field, placement, settling, slopes and breaking; fixed so that which boulders exist does not depend on the level of detail. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    manual list[ManualBoulder]

    Catalog or hand-placed boulders (ManualBoulder) placed as given.
    patches BoulderPatches

    Patches of richer and poorer boulder cover across the ground.
    pose BoulderPose

    How the boulders sit on the ground: heights, burial, lean.
    rendering BoulderRendering

    How the boulders are drawn: relief or models, and shapes.
    seed int

    Seed of the boulders, their attributes and the patches; changing it gives a different boulder field of the same statistics.
    sizes BoulderSizes

    Sizes of the boulders between craters.
    slope_map SizeSlopeMap | None

    (self) -> terraingen._terraingen.SizeSlopeMap | None
    source_resolves_px float | None

    Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the boulders (the smaller of this and completeness when both are set), by their diameter: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive. Unit: px.
    ventifacts BoulderVentifacts

    Windward facets planed on boulders by sand-laden wind, from wear; off unless share is set.

    bedrock: BoulderBedrock

    Extra boulders where the ground beneath is bedrock.

    cache_boulders: int

    Most generated boulders the layer keeps cached between queries.

    clusters: BoulderClusters

    Clusters of the boulders between craters around scattered centers; off unless share is set.

    BoulderStyle ¶

    BoulderStyle()

    One kind of boulder: its solid, stretched to axes 1 : intermediate : short_axis, rounded toward an ellipsoid by rounding, roughened by noise and cut by fracture planes; weight is its share of boulders.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    edge_softness ValueRange

    Range of how far edges and corners are worn back where faces meet, as weathering rounds them, in long-axis lengths from 0 to 0.5; 0 keeps them sharp.
    face_roughness float

    How far fracture faces undulate, as a share of each plane's offset; 0 keeps them flat. Must be from 0 to 0.5.
    fracture_depth ValueRange

    Range of where each fracture plane lies, as a share of the shape's reach along its normal, within (0, 1]; lower values cut more away.
    intermediate ValueRange

    Range of the intermediate axis over the long one, b / a, within (0, 1]; lower values give more elongated boulders.
    max_fracture_tilt float

    Largest vertical component of a fracture plane's unit normal: 0 keeps normals horizontal, cutting a slab about its rim only. Must be from 0 to 1.
    max_fractures int

    Most flat fracture planes cutting a boulder; at least the fewest. Must be from 0 to 64.
    min_fractures int

    Fewest flat fracture planes cutting a boulder; each boulder's count is drawn between the two. Must be from 0 to 64.
    name str

    Label of the style, for reference; it does not change the shapes.
    noise_amplitude float

    Largest relative change of the radius by the roughening noise; 0 leaves the surface unroughened. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    noise_octaves int

    Octaves of the roughening noise, each halving in wavelength; more add finer detail. Must be from 1 to 12.
    noise_wavelength float

    Wavelength of the roughening noise's first octave, in long-axis lengths; smaller values give finer bumps. Must be positive.
    rounding ValueRange

    Range of the share, from 0 to 1, by which the shape is rounded toward the ellipsoid of its axes: 0 keeps the solid's edges and corners, 1 is the ellipsoid.
    short_axis ValueRange

    Range of the short, vertical axis over the long one, c / a, within (0, 1] and at most the intermediate ratio; lower values give flatter boulders.
    solid BaseSolid

    Solid the shape starts from, before it is stretched, rounded, roughened and fractured.
    weight float

    Relative share of boulders given this style; the styles' weights must not all be 0. Must not be negative.

    BoulderVentifacts ¶

    BoulderVentifacts()

    Windward facets planed on share of the boulders by wind blowing toward wind_azimuth_deg, sloping min_angle_deg to max_angle_deg, with keels on keel_share of them toward second_wind_azimuth_deg; angles in degrees.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    keel_share float

    Share of faceted boulders with the second facet. Gale crater: 12 of 39 (Bridges et al. 2014). Must be from 0 to 1.
    max_angle_deg float

    Steepest facet slope from horizontal, in degrees. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    min_angle_deg float

    Gentlest facet slope from horizontal, in degrees; 50 to 60 on basalt (Laity and Bridges 2009). Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    second_wind_azimuth_deg float | None

    ChainSeamMode ¶

    Bases: enum.Enum

    How a source chain joins a source to the gaps of those before it.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    FEATHER

    Adds the height difference at the nearest edge post to the later source, fading it to 0 across width_m of the gap: the cheapest, without a solve.
    HEIGHT

    Shifts the later source by the edge's height difference spread smoothly into the gap, fading out over decay_length_m beyond an open edge: heights meet (C0), keeping the later source's relief.
    NONE

    Each cell takes the first source with data, unchanged: a step where a gap begins.
    SLOPE

    As height, with a biharmonic spread that matches slopes at the edge as well (C1).

    FEATHER class-attribute ¶

    FEATHER = 1

    Adds the height difference at the nearest edge post to the later source, fading it to 0 across width_m of the gap: the cheapest, without a solve.

    HEIGHT class-attribute ¶

    HEIGHT = 2

    Shifts the later source by the edge's height difference spread smoothly into the gap, fading out over decay_length_m beyond an open edge: heights meet (C0), keeping the later source's relief.

    NONE class-attribute ¶

    NONE = 0

    Each cell takes the first source with data, unchanged: a step where a gap begins.

    SLOPE class-attribute ¶

    SLOPE = 3

    As height, with a biharmonic spread that matches slopes at the edge as well (C1).

    decay_length float

    Length in meters over which height and slope fade the shift out where a gap is open, beyond a source's edge; it is 0 from three decay lengths on. A hole much narrower than it takes the whole shift. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    mode ChainSeamMode

    How each source meets the gaps of those before it: none switches outright, feather fades the edge's height difference out across the gap, height shifts the later source to meet the earlier one's heights (C0) and slope to meet its heights and slopes (C1). The match is solved on the posts of the source before each gap.
    width float

    Width in meters of the band inside a gap over which feather fades the height difference at the edge to 0. Must be positive. Unit: m.

    CraterAlbedoOptions ¶

    CraterAlbedoOptions()

    Which craters get bright material (selection, share), how much brighter their interiors and ejecta are in optical maturity, their rays, and how fast it all fades.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    background_maturity float

    Optical maturity (OMAT) of the ground around the craters; the excesses are added to it and the albedo is brightened from it. Must be positive.
    ejecta_excess float

    Optical maturity above the background on a fresh crater's continuous ejecta at the rim, falling with distance. Must not be negative.
    ejecta_exponent float

    Exponent of the ejecta's fall with distance r, as (r / R)^-exponent for crater radius R; higher values keep the bright ejecta nearer the rim. Must be positive.
    ejecta_reach_radii float

    Distance from the center, in crater radii, at which the ejecta's excess reaches 0. Must be above 1.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How bright material of craters too small to resolve at the sample spacing fades out.
    fade_exponent float

    Exponent of the fade with age t, max(0, 1 - t / T)^exponent for retention time T; 1 is a straight fade and higher values fade sooner. Must be positive.
    interior_excess float

    Optical maturity above the background inside a fresh crater's rim; higher values give brighter interiors. Must not be negative.
    max_maturity float

    Cap on the optical maturity where craters' excesses add up, at least the background; it limits how bright overlapping craters get.
    origin_reflectance float

    Reflectance of the optical maturity origin, the hypermature end-member, from which reflectance scales with maturity at fixed iron content.
    rays CraterRays

    Rays of bright material running out from the craters.
    retention RayRetention

    How long craters of each diameter keep their bright material.
    seed int

    Seed of which craters get bright material, their rays and their impacts; changing it gives a different pattern of the same statistics.
    selection CraterSelection

    The selection of craters given bright material: their diameters and ages, and whether manual craters count.
    share float

    Share of eligible craters given bright material. Must be from 0 to 1.
    texture CraterAlbedoTexture

    Filaments, lobed ejecta edges and walls brighter than floors; off unless streaks, lobes or a floor share below 1 are set.
    zones CraterReflectanceZones

    Bright and dark reflectance zones around new small craters, after Robinson et al. (2015) and Speyerer et al. (2016); off by default.

    How craters are applied: the datum interiors are cut relative to (fit over datum_fit_radii radii; with none, craters are added to the terrain and the settings after it are unused), how much of the interior replaces the older relief (interior_replacement, 0 to 1), the blend into the exterior, the order overlapping craters are applied in, the resolution fade, rim irregularity, rim_smoothing, noise, texture and slope.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    blend CraterBlend

    Where and how a crater's replaced interior blends into the surrounding terrain.
    datum CraterDatum

    Reference surface each crater's interior is cut relative to, fitted to the ground beneath it; none adds craters onto the terrain everywhere.
    datum_fit_radii float

    Radius of the footprint the datum is fitted over, in crater radii. Must be positive.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How craters too small to resolve fade out, by output samples (pixels) across their diameter: absent up to the first count, whole from the second.
    interior_replacement float

    Share of the interior replaced by datum plus profile: 1 erases older relief inside the crater for a clean cut, 0 keeps it on the floor and walls. Must be from 0 to 1.
    irregularity CraterIrregularity

    Irregular, non-circular crater outlines: which craters have them and how their shapes are drawn.
    noise CraterNoise

    Fractal noise over each crater's footprint and around its rim, keyed to the crater; off unless an amplitude is set.
    order CraterOrder

    Order in which overlapping craters are applied; later craters overprint earlier ones.
    peaks CraterPeaks

    Central peaks of complex craters built from massifs, lowering as the craters wear.
    replacement CraterReplacement

    How manual craters with replace set replace the terrain beneath them, whatever the datum: in full to start_radii, blending out to end_radii, on a plane fitted on a ring beyond.
    rim_smoothing RimSmoothing

    Rounded rims: each crater's profile smoothed across distance near its rim; off unless sigma_radii is set.
    slope CraterSlopeResponse

    Craters on sloping ground with floors offset downslope and rims lowered upslope; needs the plane datum.
    terraces CraterTerraces

    Slump terraces on the walls of craters from the onset diameter, softening as they wear.
    texture CraterTexture

    Gullies down fresh walls, textured ejecta and older relief buried under the ejecta; off unless an amplitude or mantling is set.

    CraterGenerationOptions ¶

    CraterGenerationOptions()

    Which craters are generated: diameters from min_diameter to max_diameter (m), kept apart by spacing, at most max_craters (None for no cap), plus manual ones.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    cell_size_factor float

    Side of the cells craters are drawn in, as a multiple of each band's largest diameter. Must be positive.
    completeness SurfaceField

    Diameter (m) from which manual is a complete catalog at each point, or from which a DEM resolves craters (source_resolved_limit).
    keep_share Callable[[Crater], float]

    Callable giving the share of generated craters like a Crater kept, by a uniform keyed to each ID; it is called from worker threads.
    manual list[Crater]

    Hand-placed craters, kept whatever the density.
    margin_radii float

    Also keeps craters centered outside the region within this many of their radii of it. Must not be negative.
    max_band_diameter float

    Bands whose craters are all larger than this, in meters, are skipped unless spacing or a cap is on; infinity generates every band. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    max_craters int | None

    Most generated craters kept, the largest first; unset keeps all. Manual craters are always kept, and a cap means tiles no longer match the whole grid.
    max_diameter float

    Largest crater generated, in meters; above the smallest. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    max_expected_craters float

    Most craters a generation may expect, to catch requests that would exhaust memory. Must not be negative.
    min_diameter float

    Smallest crater generated, in meters; lower values add many more small craters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    min_resolved_diameter float

    Bands whose craters are all smaller than this, in meters, are skipped; 0 generates every band. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    spacing CraterSpacing

    Keeps craters of similar size apart by removing conflicting ones, which lowers the density below the model's.
    threads int

    Threads the cells are drawn on; 0 for every hardware thread.

    CraterIrregularity ¶

    CraterIrregularity()

    Irregular, elongated crater outlines for the craters it selects: rims roughened by random harmonics and some craters stretched into ellipses.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    ellipticity ValueDistribution

    Long over short rim-to-rim diameter of elliptical craters, drawn per crater; at least 1.
    elongated_share float

    Share of eligible craters made elliptical, keeping their area. Must be from 0 to 1.
    enabled bool

    Gives eligible craters irregular, non-circular outlines; off keeps every crater round.
    heading_deg float | None

    Heading of elliptical craters' long axes, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); unset gives random headings. Unit: deg.
    heading_spread_deg float

    Largest random turn of a long axis either way from the heading, in degrees. Must not be negative. Unit: deg.
    marks_amplitude ValueDistribution

    Largest radial shift of the wall by the marks, in crater radii, drawn per crater; below marks_fade_radii / 3.75.
    marks_fade_radii float

    Width, in crater radii, over which the marks fade in and out. Must be above 0 and at most 0.5.
    marks_inner_radii float

    Distance from the center, in crater radii, where the marks reach full strength. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    marks_knots int

    Random shifts around the crater the marks pass through; more knots give narrower marks. Must be from 3 to 1024.
    marks_outer_radii float

    Distance from the center, in crater radii, where the marks start to fade; at most 1 minus marks_fade_radii. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    marks_share float

    Share of eligible craters given radial marks: ridges and grooves down the wall, strongest where it is steepest. Must be from 0 to 1.
    max_deviation float

    With du_2024, the largest deviation of a rim from a circle, in radii; outlines beyond it are scaled down to it. Must be above 0 and at most 0.5.
    max_harmonic int

    With power_law, the highest harmonic of the rim's waviness; higher harmonics add finer wiggles. Must be from 1 to 64.
    min_harmonic int

    With power_law, the lowest harmonic of the rim's waviness. Must be from 1 to 64.
    model RimRoughnessModel

    How rough rims are drawn.
    rough_share float

    Share of eligible craters given rough, wavy rims. Must be from 0 to 1.
    roughness ValueDistribution

    With power_law, the RMS deviation of a rough rim from a circle, in crater radii, drawn per crater.
    scatter bool

    With du_2024, scatters each crater's spectrum by the fits' measured misfits and noise.
    seed int | None

    Seed the outlines are drawn with, along with each crater's ID; changing it reshapes every irregular crater. Unset follows the layer's seed.
    selection CraterSelection

    The selection of craters made irregular: their diameters and ages, and whether manual craters count.
    spectral_slope ValueDistribution

    With power_law, the exponent s of the rim harmonics' amplitudes, falling as k^-s, drawn per crater; higher values leave less fine waviness.

    CraterNoise()

    Fractal noise added to each crater, keyed to its ID: amplitude over the whole footprint (fading out beyond the rim) at wavelength_radii, and rim_amplitude in the band from rim_inner_radii to rim_outer_radii at rim_wavelength_radii; amplitudes are shares of the diameter and 0 adds none.

    Amplitude of the noise over the whole footprint, as a share of the crater diameter; it fades out beyond the rim to the profile's reach, and 0 adds none. Must not be negative.

    Weight ratio between successive octaves. Must be positive.
    octaves int

    Octaves of both noises. Must be from 1 to 12.

    rim_outer_radii float

    chain_spread_deg float

    Spread of the lesser massifs' bearings about a chain through the center, in degrees: about 70 strings them across the floor, wide spreads scatter them around it into stars and crosses. Must be from 0 to 360 deg. Unit: deg.
    elongation float

    Most aspect ratio of a massif's footprint; 1 keeps them round, larger makes ridges. Must be from 1 to 4.

    Builds the central peaks of complex craters from massifs: mountains clustered about the center in place of the profile's round dome.

    lopsidedness float

    max_massifs int

    min_massifs int

    Fewest massifs of a peak. Must be from 1 to 8.
    roughness float

    Ridged noise over the massifs, as a share of their height, carving spurs, gullies and lesser summits; worn peaks lose it. Must be from 0 to 1.
    roughness_wavelength float

    Varies each crater's massifs and their noise; unset follows the layer's seed.

    warp float

    How far the noise warps the massifs' outlines, in peak base radii. Must be from 0 to 0.3.
    width_scale float

    The massifs' spread and size over the profile's peak base. Must be above 0 and at most 3.

    CraterProfile ¶

    CraterProfile()

    A crater's height relative to the surrounding surface at distance meters from its center. Subclass it and implement height(distance, diameter, state) and reach_radii() (how far, in radii, it changes the terrain), and optionally is_complex(diameter). A Python profile is called for every sample near every crater, from every evaluation thread, and Python calls take turns on the GIL, so evaluate terrains with one on one thread (threads=1).

    Name Type Description
    count ValueDistribution

    Number of rays of a crater, drawn per crater and rounded; from 0 to 64.
    enabled bool

    Gives craters rays of bright material; off leaves only their interiors and ejecta bright.
    excess float

    Optical maturity above the background along a ray at the rim, falling linearly to 0 at its end; higher values give brighter rays. Must not be negative.
    layout RayLayout | None

    Takes the rays' number, directions and widths from this layout in place of count and width_deg, so they lie over a secondaries layer with the same layout; unset draws them per crater.
    length_coefficient float

    Coefficient of the median ray length, coefficient R^exponent km for crater radius R in km; higher values give longer rays. Must be positive.
    length_exponent float

    Exponent of the crater radius in the median ray length; higher values make large craters' rays relatively longer. Must be positive.
    length_spread ValueDistribution

    Natural logarithm of a ray's length over the median, drawn per ray; a wider distribution gives more varied lengths.
    oblique ObliqueImpacts

    How oblique impacts lengthen rays downrange and clear them uprange.
    patch_radii float

    Wavelength of the noise along a ray, in crater radii; smaller values give shorter patches. Must be positive.
    patchiness float

    Share of a ray's strength that noise along it can take away, breaking it into patches; 0 gives unbroken rays. Must be from 0 to 1.
    width_deg ValueDistribution

    Angle in degrees a ray spans 2 radii from the center, drawn per ray, within (0, 180); beyond 2 radii a ray keeps the width it has there.

    CraterSlopeResponse ¶

    CraterSlopeResponse()

    Craters made asymmetric along the slope of the ground beneath their layer: the deepest point floor_offset diameters downslope (drawn per crater), upslope_rim of the raised rim and ejecta kept upslope, complete from full_slope_deg degrees.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    asymmetric bool

    Shapes craters asymmetrically along the slope of the ground beneath the layer; off keeps them the same on any slope.
    critical_gradient float | None

    Critical gradient Sc, rise over run, toward which downslope transport grows without bound: a crater on a regional gradient S wears 1 / (1 - (S / Sc)^2) times as fast (Roering et al. 1999). Unset wears craters alike on any slope; no lunar value is published. Must be positive.
    floor_offset ValueDistribution

    How far the deepest point lies downslope of the center, in diameters, drawn per crater; below 0.23.
    full_slope_deg float

    Slope at which the asymmetry is complete, in degrees; it rises from none on level ground. Must be positive. Unit: deg.
    max_wear_rate float

    Fastest a slope makes craters wear, over level ground: a numerical cap as S nears Sc. Must be at least 1.
    seed int | None

    Varies how far each crater's floor is offset; unset follows the layer's seed.
    upslope_rim float

    Share of the raised rim and ejecta kept straight upslope; the rest returns toward the sides. Must be from 0 to 1.

    asymmetric property ¶

    asymmetric: bool

    Shapes craters asymmetrically along the slope of the ground beneath the layer; off keeps them the same on any slope.

    critical_gradient property ¶

    critical_gradient: float | None

    Critical gradient Sc, rise over run, toward which downslope transport grows without bound: a crater on a regional gradient S wears 1 / (1 - (S / Sc)^2) times as fast (Roering et al. 1999). Unset wears craters alike on any slope; no lunar value is published. Must be positive.

    floor_offset property ¶

    floor_offset: ValueDistribution

    How far the deepest point lies downslope of the center, in diameters, drawn per crater; below 0.23.

    full_slope_deg property ¶

    full_slope_deg: float

    Slope at which the asymmetry is complete, in degrees; it rises from none on level ground. Must be positive. Unit: deg.

    max_wear_rate property ¶

    max_wear_rate: float

    Fastest a slope makes craters wear, over level ground: a numerical cap as S nears Sc. Must be at least 1.

    seed property ¶

    Varies how far each crater's floor is offset; unset follows the layer's seed.

    upslope_rim property ¶

    Share of the raised rim and ejecta kept straight upslope; the rest returns toward the sides. Must be from 0 to 1.

    validate

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    arc_share float

    Share of the wall's circumference each bench covers at the onset diameter; it rises to 0.9 at the full diameter, and 1 gives benches all the way round. Must be above 0 and at most 1.
    bench_slope_deg float

    Slope of a bench, in degrees; mapped lunar terraces slope under 5 degrees. Must be above 0 and below 45 deg. Unit: deg.
    block_gaps float

    Share of slump blocks missing from each bench, breaking the benches into segments. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    block_offset float

    How far each slump block's headscarp steps from its neighbors', as a share of the room between scarps. Must be from 0 to 1.
    enabled bool

    Steps the walls of large craters into slump terraces: benches and scarps between the floor and the rim crest.
    full_diameter float

    Diameter in meters from which every crater has its most benches, over most of its wall; above the onset diameter. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    max_benches int

    Benches from the full diameter; complex lunar craters usually have more than 3. Must be from 1 to 12.
    min_benches int

    Benches at the onset diameter. Must be from 1 to 12.
    min_freshness float

    Freshness, current over fresh depth, below which the terraces are gone; they soften as the crater wears down to it. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    onset_diameter float

    Smallest terraced crater, in meters; 20 km on the Moon, where half of fresh mare craters are terraced, and about 8 km on Mars. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    rim_variation float

    How far the bench radii wander around the rim, in crater radii. Must not be negative.
    scarp_share float

    Least share of each step's width the scarps take; steeper steps give them more, and the bench takes the rest. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    scarp_slope_deg float

    Slope the scarps rise at, in degrees, above the bench slope; each step gives its scarps the share of its width that keeps them near it. Must be above 0 and below 60 deg. Unit: deg.
    seed int | None

    Varies each crater's benches, the arcs they cover and how they wander; unset follows the layer's seed.

    DiamondSquareOptions ¶

    DiamondSquareOptions()

    The fractal diamond-square refines posts with: fractal_dimension and scale (meters; None estimates them from the posts), fit_window_px (side in posts of the overlapping windows a None scale is fitted over, so each region follows its own roughness; 0 fits one scale to the posts), interp, min_pixel_size (posts' units, 0 for no limit) and seed.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    fit_window_px int

    Side in posts of the overlapping windows, centered every half side, that an unset scale_m is fitted over; each node's scale is bilinear between the windows around it. 0 fits one scale to a sample of the posts; else at least 4. Must be from 0 to 1024 px. Unit: px.
    fractal_dimension float | None

    Fractal dimension, 2 smooth and 3 rough: each square or diamond step scales the displacement by 2^-((3 - F) / 2). Unset estimates it from the median height differences of the posts at lags of 1 to 8 posts. Must be from 2 to 3.
    interp DiamondSquareInterp

    How new nodes are filled from the coarser ones and samples read between the finest nodes.
    min_pixel_size float

    Finest node spacing in meters the posts are refined to; 0 refines down to the sample spacing. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    scale float | None

    Displacement standard deviation in meters at the posts' last step; unset estimates it per fit_window_px window. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    seed int

    Seed of the displacements.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    anchor tuple[float, float]

    On a body, the longitude and latitude in degrees of the point whose tangent frame the dunes are laid out in; they are true to scale near it and absent on the far hemisphere.
    azimuth_spread_deg float

    Largest difference of each barchan or dome's wind from the azimuth, in degrees. Must not be negative. Unit: deg.
    defect_density float

    Transverse, barchanoid and linear dunes: pairs of crest ends per meter of crest, so crests break into segments about 1 / defect_density long; 0 for none. Olympia Undae: 0.0027 (Ewing et al. 2010). Must not be negative. Unit: 1/m.
    defects float

    Transverse, barchanoid and linear dunes: share of the height that varies along crests, lowering and ending some. Must be from 0 to 1.
    density float

    Barchans and domes: chance a cell holds a dune. Must be from 0 to 1.
    dome_exponent float

    Exponent alpha of the cos^alpha profile of domes. Must be positive.
    dome_length float

    Domes: length along the wind over width. Must be positive.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How dunes too fine for the sample spacing fade out, by samples across their width or wavelength.
    flank_slope_deg float

    Linear dunes: mean slope of both flanks, in degrees. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    grainflows DuneGrainflows | None

    Grainflows on the slip faces: scarps below the brink and lobes below them; unset for none.
    height float

    Transverse, barchanoid and linear dunes: crest height, in meters. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    height_ratio float

    Barchans and domes: height over width. Must be positive.
    horn_length float

    Barchans: how far the horns reach downwind of the crest, in dune heights. Must not be negative.
    lattice_spacing float

    Barchans and domes: side of the lattice cells, each holding at most one dune, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    min_width float

    Barchans: width in meters below which a dune is a dome without a slip face, blending into barchans up to 1.5 times it. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    ripples DuneRipples | None

    Ripples superposed on the dunes; unset for none.
    seed int

    Seed of the dunes and ripples; changing it gives a different layout of the same statistics.
    shape DuneShape

    The kind of dune.
    sinuosity float

    Transverse, barchanoid and linear dunes: how far a crest wanders along its length, in wavelengths. Must not be negative.
    slip_face_angle_deg float

    Slope of the lee slip faces, in degrees: the sand's angle of repose. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    source_resolves_px float | None

    Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the dunes, their ripples and grainflows, by their width or crest wavelength, ripple wavelength and narrowest lobe: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive. Unit: px.
    stoss_exponent float

    Exponent alpha of the cos^alpha windward profile of dunes; higher is blunter. Must be positive.
    stoss_slope_deg float

    Mean slope of the windward faces, in degrees; below the slip face angle. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    wavelength float

    Transverse, barchanoid and linear dunes: crest-to-crest spacing, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    width float

    Barchans and domes: mean width, horn to horn, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    width_spread float

    Barchans and domes: each width varies from (1 - spread) to (1 + spread) times the mean. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    wind_azimuth_deg float

    Direction the wind blows toward, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); slip faces face it. Unit: deg.

    DuneRipples ¶

    DuneRipples()

    Ripples on dunes: wavelength and height (m) on flat sand, turned and tightened by the dune's slope by slope_coupling; DuneOptions.ripples None gives none.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    defect_density float

    Forked crests (Y-junctions): pairs of crest ends per meter of crest, as measured on dune fields (Ewing et al. 2010); 0 for none. Mars large ripples: 0.099. Must not be negative. Unit: 1/m.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How ripples too fine for the sample spacing fade out, by samples per wavelength.
    flank_straightening float

    How far crests straighten off the stoss: 1 keeps the sinuosity on flat sand and stoss slopes and takes it away on flanks and lee slopes, as Martian large ripples do. Must be from 0 to 1.
    height float

    Trough-to-crest height of the ripples on flat sand, in meters. Must not be negative. Unit: m.
    interdune_cover float

    Share of the ripple height kept on the ground between dunes. Must be from 0 to 1.
    lee_fraction float

    Share of a ripple wavelength the lee face takes: 0.5 is symmetric, lower values give a steeper lee face. Must be above 0 and below 1.
    sinuosity float

    How far a ripple crest wanders along its length, in wavelengths. Must not be negative.
    slope_coupling float

    How strongly the dune's slope turns and tightens the ripples: they shorten on steep lee faces and turn on the flanks; 0 keeps them straight across the wind. Must not be negative.
    wavelength float

    Crest-to-crest spacing of the ripples on flat sand, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.

    DuneShape ¶

    Bases: enum.Enum

    The kind of dune a DuneLayer builds.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    BARCHAN

    Isolated crescents with a slip face and horns downwind; domes below min_width_m.
    BARCHANOID

    Transverse crests bent into linked crescents, as where sand supply rises.
    DOME

    Isolated rounded heaps without a slip face.
    LINEAR

    Symmetric crests along the wind, as under two winds on scarce sand.
    TRANSVERSE

    Continuous crests across the wind, each with a slip face.

    FractalType ¶

    Bases: enum.Enum

    How octaves of the basis noise are combined.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    BILLOW

    Sum of absolute-value octaves: rounded, puffy forms.
    FBM

    Fractional Brownian motion: a weighted sum of octaves, the general-purpose choice.
    HYBRID_MULTIFRACTAL

    Hybrid multifractal: smooth lowlands and rough highlands.
    RIDGED

    Ridged multifractal: sharp crests from inverted absolute noise, like eroded ridges.

    GeoTiffSource ¶

    GeoTiffSource()

    Bases: terraingen._terraingen.Source

    Heights from band band of a GeoTIFF, scaled (height * scale + offset), its cells refined by upsampler (cubic when None). A projected file suits a plane terrain and one in longitude and latitude a terrain on a body, its crop and cell sizes in degrees. The file is decoded a tile or strip at a time as heights are asked of them and kept in a cache of at most cache_bytes, so a small area of a file too large for memory reads only the blocks around it. With crop (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y) it covers only the cells meeting that box, giving the same heights there as without it. effective_pixel_size is the cell size the heights truly resolve, for a DEM upsampled before it was saved.

    init(self, path: str | os.PathLike, band: int = 0, scale: float | None = None, offset: float | None = None, crop: tuple[float, float, float, float] | None = None, effective_pixel_size: float | None = None, upsampler: terraingen._terraingen.Upsampler | None = None, cache_bytes: int = 536870912) -> None

    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    burial float | None

    Buried share of the height; unset draws it. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    diameter float

    Length of the long axis, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    height float | None

    Vertical extent in meters, buried part included; unset draws it from the height ratios. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    id int | None

    Stable ID that seeds what is drawn for the boulder; unset derives one from its position and diameter.
    lean_deg float | None

    Tilt of the boulder's vertical axis from the vertical, degrees; unset draws it. Unit: deg.
    model bool | None

    Whether it is a 3D model rather than relief in the heights; unset follows the layer's model threshold.
    rest BoulderRest | None

    Which axis it stands along; unset draws it. A fixed lean, tilt, tilt azimuth or rest keeps a model from being tipped over by settle.
    shape_seed int | None

    Seed of its 3D shape, as a generated boulder's derived one; unset derives it from the ID.
    tilt_azimuth_deg float | None

    Direction the up axis tips toward, degrees counter-clockwise from east; unset draws it. Unit: deg.
    tilt_deg float | None

    Angle of the up axis from the vertical after lean, degrees; unset draws it. A followed slope tips it further. Unit: deg.
    wear float | None

    How worn it is, 0 fresh; unset draws it. With burial_by_wear it sets a drawn burial. Must be from 0 to 1.
    x float

    Center along x in the surface's coordinates; the longitude in degrees on a sphere.
    y float

    Center along y in the surface's coordinates; the latitude in degrees on a sphere.
    yaw_deg float | None

    Rotation about the vertical, degrees counter-clockwise from east; unset draws it. Unit: deg.

    Name Type Description
    PERLIN

    Improved Perlin gradient noise: smooth, general-purpose relief.
    SIMPLEX

    Simplex gradient noise: smooth relief, an alternative to Perlin.
    VALUE

    Value noise: random values interpolated over a lattice; blockier than gradient noise.
    VORONOI

    Voronoi cells, each at one random height: flat polygonal plateaus and terraces.
    WORLEY_F1

    Cellular noise from the distance to the nearest feature point: cones and basins.
    WORLEY_F2

    Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point.
    WORLEY_F2_MINUS_F1

    Cellular noise F2 - F1: ridges along cell borders, like cracked ground.

    ObliqueImpacts()

    Ray patterns of oblique impacts: below asymmetric_deg the ejecta is asymmetric, below forbidden_deg an uprange zone has no rays, below butterfly_deg rays form a butterfly; impacts come from heading_deg (degrees counter-clockwise from east) or any direction.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    asymmetric_deg float

    Impact angle from the horizontal, in degrees, below which ejecta leave faster downrange, lengthening rays there and shortening them uprange. Must be from 0 to 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    butterfly_deg float

    Impact angle in degrees below which rays within the zone half width of downrange are dropped too, a butterfly pattern; at most the forbidden angle. Must be from 0 to 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    downrange_speed_ratio ValueDistribution

    Downrange over uprange ejection speed below the asymmetric angle, drawn per crater; at least 1, higher values stretch downrange rays more.
    enabled bool

    Draws an impact angle and direction per crater that shape its rays; off treats every impact as vertical.
    forbidden_deg float

    Impact angle in degrees below which rays within the zone half width of uprange are dropped; at most the asymmetric angle. Must be from 0 to 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    heading_deg float | None

    Downrange direction of every impact, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); unset draws a random heading per crater. Unit: deg.
    zone_half_width_deg float

    Half width in degrees of the ray-free zones uprange and downrange; illustrative, as the sources do not measure it. Must be from 0 to 180 deg. Unit: deg.

    ReflectanceZone ¶

    ReflectanceZone()

    A reflectance zone around new small craters: share of craters have it, it changes reflectance by change and reaches coefficient * D^exponent m times scale, with fingers pulling in by raggedness and an edge fading over feather.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    validate

    validate(self) -> None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    change ValueDistribution

    Reflectance change relative to the pre-impact surface, drawn per crater; above -1, negative values darken.
    coefficient float

    Coefficient of the zone's reach from the crater's center, coefficient D^exponent meters for diameter D in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    exponent float

    Exponent of the diameter in the zone's reach. Must be positive.
    feather float

    Share of the reach over which the zone fades out at its edge. Must be above 0 and at most 1.
    finger_width_deg float

    Typical width of the edge's fingers around the crater, in degrees. Must be positive. Unit: deg.
    raggedness float

    Share of the reach that fingers of the edge pull in by; 0 keeps the zone round, higher values make it ray-like. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    retention_myr float | None

    How long the zone lasts, in Myr, fading like the bright material; unset lasts as long as the bright material. Must be positive. Unit: Myr.
    scale ValueDistribution

    Factor on the reach, drawn per crater; positive and bounded, a wider distribution gives more varied zones.
    share float

    Share of craters with the zone. Must be from 0 to 1.

    ResampleMethod ¶

    Bases: enum.Enum

    How a raster is interpolated.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    BILINEAR

    Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.
    CUBIC

    Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.
    CUBIC_BSPLINE

    The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves.
    LANCZOS3

    The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.
    NEAREST

    The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.

    BILINEAR class-attribute ¶

    BILINEAR = 1

    Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.

    CUBIC class-attribute ¶

    CUBIC = 2

    Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.

    CUBIC_BSPLINE class-attribute ¶

    CUBIC_BSPLINE = 4

    The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves.

    LANCZOS3 class-attribute ¶

    LANCZOS3 = 3

    The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.

    NEAREST class-attribute ¶

    The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.

    validate

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    cell_size_factor float

    Side of the polar cells secondaries are drawn in, as a multiple of each size band's largest diameter. Must be positive.
    count_fraction float

    Size, as a fraction of the primary's diameter, from which the onset count counts secondaries. Must be positive.
    max_diameter float | None

    Largest secondary generated, in meters; unset has no limit beyond Singer et al.'s largest secondary at each range. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    min_diameter float

    Smallest secondary generated, in meters. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    onset_count float | None

    Secondaries at least count_fraction primary diameters across, in an area the size of the primary at the onset range; the sources give sizes, not numbers. Must be positive. Required.
    outer_range float | None

    How far secondaries reach, in primary diameters from its center; unset uses the longest typical ray of Elliott et al. (2018). Must be positive.
    rays SecondaryRays

    Secondaries gathered into rays and clumped along them; off by default.
    seed int

    Seed the secondaries are drawn with; changing it gives a different field of the same statistics.
    selection CraterSelection

    The selection of primary craters that throw secondaries: their diameters and ages, and whether manual craters count.
    shapes SecondaryShapes

    Secondaries stretched toward their primary; round by default.
    size_slope float

    Cumulative size slope of the secondaries, their number falling as d^-slope; higher values give relatively more small secondaries. Must be positive.
    source_resolves_px float | None

    Source cells across from which the source's data already holds the secondaries, by their diameter: only smaller ones are added, each raster of a chain giving its own limit. Ignored on synthetic sources and where no raster has data; null adds them all. Must be positive. Unit: px.

    A shape-model body's own labels refined by upsampler (cubic when None): heights are the refined radius less the body's, which interpolates the labels bilinearly, so 0 at every label.     Name Type Description
    bright_change ValueDistribution

    Reflectance change of a bright splotch, drawn per splotch; above -1.
    bright_share float

    Share of splotches brighter than the ground; the rest are mixed, dark on one side and bright on the other. Must be from 0 to 1.
    dark_change ValueDistribution

    Reflectance change of a dark splotch relative to the ground before it, drawn per splotch; above -1.
    dark_share float

    Share of splotches darker than the ground. Must be from 0 to 1.
    fade ResolutionFade

    How splotches too small to resolve at the sample spacing fade out.
    lifetime_myr float

    How long a splotch lasts in Myr, fading linearly; the default is the time splotches take to churn the top centimeters. Must be positive. Unit: Myr.
    max_diameter float

    Largest splotch diameter in meters, above the smallest. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    min_diameter float

    Smallest splotch diameter in meters; the published fit is extrapolated below 10 m. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    raggedness float

    Share of a splotch's radius that lobes of its edge pull in by; 0 keeps it round. Must be from 0 to below 1.
    rate_coefficient float

    Coefficient a of the cumulative formation rate a d^-b per km^2 per year, d the diameter in km; higher values give more splotches. Must be positive.
    rate_exponent float

    Slope b of the cumulative formation rate; higher values give relatively more small splotches. Must be positive.
    seed int

    Seed of where splotches fall and what they are.
    softness float

    Share of a splotch's radius over which its edge fades. Must be above 0 and at most 1.
    steep_bright_share float | None

    Share of splotches on slopes steeper than the steep slope that are bright, read from the terrain's heights; unset keeps the bright share. Bright splotches are found mostly on such slopes, but the source gives no share. Must be from 0 to 1.
    steep_slope_deg float

    Slope in degrees from which ground is steep. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    swarms SplotchSwarms

    Swarms of splotches around new craters; off by default.

    Smallest crater with a swarm, in meters; smaller craters throw few splotches. Must be positive. Unit: m.

    Nearest landing distance in meters, setting Robinson et al.'s median of 8.7 km. Must be positive. Unit: m.

    wedge_share float

    Share of swarm splotches shaped as wedges pointing back to their crater. Illustrative. Must be from 0 to 1.

    TerrainView ¶

    TerrainView()

    A terrain's heights over one grid, for loops that edit the terrain and evaluate it again. The view keeps the heights before layer stage (None for the last layer, 0 for the source's heights), so update after replacing that layer or a later one applies only the layers from there on, and update of an unchanged terrain evaluates nothing. Updates give the bits of Terrain.evaluate.

    init(self, grid: terraingen._terraingen.RasterGrid, spacing: float = 0.0, threads: int = 0, backend: terraingen._terraingen.Backend | None = None, stage: int | None = None) -> None

    ZoneShadows ¶

    ZoneShadows()

    Shadows of rises in the distal zones: a jet from the rim that drops at most jet_angle_deg, full shadow depth m below it, sampled on azimuths rays of radial_samples.

    init(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None

    Defaults, with positional arguments setting the fields in order and each keyword the field of that name.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    azimuths int

    Rays around a crater the ground is sampled on. Must be from 8 to 8192.
    depth float

    Depth in meters of the ground below the jet at which the shadow is full. Illustrative. Must be positive. Unit: m.
    enabled bool

    Gives the distal zones shadows behind rises such as crater rims, read from the terrain's heights; off by default.
    jet_angle_deg float

    Steepest angle in degrees at which the jet forming the distal zones can drop behind a rise; lower values give longer shadows. Illustrative. Must be above 0 and below 90 deg. Unit: deg.
    radial_samples int

    Samples along each ray out to the distal zones' reach. Must be from 8 to 8192.

    The heights as a mesh, a vertex per cell with data, in the frame boulder models are written in: world coordinates on a plane, east-north-up meters of site on a sphere.
